items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol launch
items.summary: OpenAI priced Sol at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens, compared with $10/$50 for Astra ( pricing summary ). Claimed results : It reportedly beats GPT-6 Sol by 6.4 points on DeepSWE v1.1 and Opus 5.5 by 2.2 points on AutomationBench ( summary ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: Agent Arena placements
items.summary: Sol [Max] entered at #5 (+11.23%) with a $0.56 median cost per task ( @arena ). Sol cost comparison : That is 39% cheaper than GPT-6 Sol while scoring 1.52 points higher. It is 81% cheaper than Astra while landing within 1.04 points.

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: Code and Text Arena
items.summary: Sol briefly entered WebDev at #3 before Sonnet 5.5 pushed it to #4 ( weekly recap ). Sonnet on WebDev : Sonnet now sits 2 points behind GPT-6 Astra [Max] at 80% lower cost.

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: Other independent evals
items.summary: WeirdML v3 finds Sol very token-efficient, close to Astra but with a lower peak. On the same benchmark, Sonnet 5.5 beats Opus 5 and Grok 4.7 beats Kimi-K3; these results are incomplete ( @htihle ). Reasoning style : Design Arena read 324 thinking summaries.

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: Step 5 Preview
items.summary: StepFun’s model ranks #7 among open-weight models on Vals at $2.54 per task. It averages nearly two hours per task and has a 1M-token context window ( Vals , details ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: Rumors (unconfirmed)
items.summary: Fable 5.5 : Claude Fable 5.5 is rumored for next week and said to outperform an “Astra 6.1” that was reportedly delayed over security concerns. The poster says he cannot verify either claim ( @kimmonismus , follow-up ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: GPT-6 Astra Lite
items.summary: A “GPT-6 Astra Lite” listing has been spotted, which @scaling01 speculates is the same model as Sol ( @scaling01 ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: Decision models and open weights
items.summary: llama.cpp added a /v1/systemone endpoint for local “Jev-style” decision-model inference ( @ggerganov ). Running locally : Models are launched with llama serve -hf ggml-org/Kev-4B-GGUF ( @ClementDelangue ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: Skeptical view
items.summary: @mervenoyann calls decision models a rebrand of zero-shot classifiers ( tweet ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: Calibration analysis
items.summary: A blog post links Jev-style calibration to value and Q-function prediction ( @SOURADIPCHAKR18 ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 Reshape the Cost–Performance Frontier
items.title: webAI TwIL-LM3-Pro
items.summary: This 3.66B model is post-trained from Granite 4.2. In webAI’s tests it roughly matches Qwen3-8B on formal logic. The Q4 GGUF is 2.09 GiB and the license is non-commercial ( @kimmonismus ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, Assistants and Developer Tooling
items.title: Muse Gadgets
items.summary: Meta open-sourced ESP32 firmware and a Linux SDK for building hardware that works with Muse ( @natfriedman ). Muse Home Link : Meta made 5,000 units of its own smart-home bridge, free for subscribers while supplies last ( @alexandr_wang , shipping ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, Assistants and Developer Tooling
items.title: Extensible harnesses
items.summary: DeepSeek Harness shipped desktop builds for macOS and Windows; Linux users install @deepseek-ai/dsh from npm ( @deepseek_ai ). Claude Code mods : Mods are plugins with middleware-like hooks into Claude Code ( @lydiahallie ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, Assistants and Developer Tooling
items.title: T3 Code orchestrator rewrite
items.summary: The project passed 400K users ( @theo ). Its 4-month PR, with 823 commits across 1,912 files, has now merged ( @maria_rcks ). New features : The rewrite adds Pi support, cross-provider delegate_task , an ACP registry, thread forking, mid-thread model switching…

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, Assistants and Developer Tooling
items.title: Platform updates
items.summary: OpenAI’s Agents API added one-call browser computer use, Bedrock Managed Agents and portable environments. It also claims 99.97% turn reliability and 20% faster tool calls ( @stevendcoffey ).

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: Multi-harness RL (Hugging Face)
items.summary: The same model weights score 62% in one harness and 33% in another ( @huggingface ). Method : A proxy speaks the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini API formats and records sampled token IDs and logprobs for training, with no changes to the harnesses themselves.

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: Credit assignment and RL efficiency
items.summary: ProVer has a judge locate the decisive trajectory segment, then uses rollouts on either side to set that segment’s advantage. It reports +9.91% (Qwen3.5-2B) and +7.12% (Qwen3.5-4B) relative gains over GRPO ( @omarsar0 ).

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: Frontier Learning
items.summary: The method targets problems at the edge of capability, since problems a model always or never solves give zero GRPO gradient ( @robinfaro13 ).

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: Sharpening Tax
items.summary: The paper quantifies the loss of pass@K scalability after post-training and proposes PTGS, a per-prompt temperature sampler ( @iScienceLuvr ).

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: Long-horizon control and context
items.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs reports that a dedicated controller lifts GPT-5.5 on ProgramBench from 63.7% to 71.5%, using the same workers and budget, versus 58.0% for Codex ( @dair_ai ).

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: Long-context degradation
items.summary: NVIDIA’s Long-Transduction study measures a 62.8% accuracy drop from 4K to 128K context across seven open models ( @dair_ai ).

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: Multi-agent coordination
items.summary: In AgentWorld, fewer than a third of multi-agent actions help complete the task, and coordination tasks reach only 12% success ( @omarsar0 ).

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: Apple LoopCD
items.summary: The method halves recurrent loops while raising AIME 2024 pass@1 from 61.88% to 73.33% ( @arankomatsuzaki ).

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: AI on open math problems
items.summary: Meta released six papers on open problems produced with Muse Spark 1.1 and 1.2 through plain meta.ai chat, with no custom scaffold ( @AIatMeta , list ).

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: Google Cogentic
items.summary: This Gemini multi-agent system produced new results on five open theory problems ( @omarsar0 ).

items.subsection: Research: Agent Training, Long-Horizon Control and AI for Math
items.title: Image post-training
items.summary: Arena combined a Bradley-Terry reward model with faithfulness, constraint and anti-reward-hacking rewards ( @arena ). Results : FLUX.2-dev gained 69 Elo to 1202, and Ideogram 4 gained 20 Elo to 1224.

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Eval Integrity and Safety
items.title: Research-taste benchmarks
items.summary: ScholarCatalyst asks agents to find the “catalyst papers” behind research projects. It is labeled by 184 lead authors on 207 of their own projects and is described as far from saturated ( @yoonholeee ).

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Eval Integrity and Safety
items.title: Vals Web Search Index
items.summary: The index holds model and harness constant, swaps only the search tool, and scores final answers on finance and legal tasks ( @ValsAI ). Validation : Agents score 2.9% (legal) and 7.4% (finance) without search, versus 30–50% with it.

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Eval Integrity and Safety
items.title: SWE bug-finding bench
items.summary: In this new benchmark, agents start from an older commit and are scored against real bugs fixed in later commits. Critique : Lucas Beyer argues it mainly tests recall and that the construction is easy to train toward ( @giffmana ).

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Eval Integrity and Safety
items.title: Authors’ response
items.summary: The authors say training for bug-finding is fine as long as the test set is excluded ( @OfirPress ).

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Eval Integrity and Safety
items.title: Eval integrity question
items.summary: David Rein asks whether Harbor, the framework behind Terminal Bench, lets agents modify their trajectories before evaluation. He notes he may be misreading the code ( @idavidrein ).

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Eval Integrity and Safety
items.title: Offensive capability of open models
items.summary: The Batch reports GLM-5.3 nearly matched Claude Mythos at exploiting vulnerabilities, 12% vs 14% ( @DeepLearningAI ). Disputed claim : One commentator says GLM-5.3 Flash exceeds Mythos Preview on ExploitBench ( @teortaxesTex ).

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Eval Integrity and Safety
items.title: Uncensored variant
items.summary: An uncensored GLM-5.3 is circulating on Hugging Face ( @kimmonismus ).

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Eval Integrity and Safety
items.title: Safety research and safeguards
items.summary: A new paper proposes using internal signals during training to improve alignment without degrading white-box monitoring ( @lenalibon ).

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Eval Integrity and Safety
items.title: False positives
items.summary: Opus 5.5 frequently triggers “reasoning extraction” safeguards during spectrogram syllable labeling ( @ChaseBrowe32432 ).

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Eval Integrity and Safety
items.title: Emergent world knowledge
items.summary: Asking a model “land or water?” for 16,200 lat/long coordinates and plotting the answers yields a recognizable world map ( @karpathy ).

items.subsection: Inference, Hardware and Systems
items.title: Ascend 950 via DeepSeek kernels
items.summary: An analysis of DeepSeek’s open-sourced DeepGEMM, FlashMLA, TileKernels and DeepEP infers the chip’s layout ( @ZhihuFrontier ). Estimated specs : The chip has 32 AI cores, each pairing one Cube core with two Vector cores.

items.subsection: Inference, Hardware and Systems
items.title: Prime Inference
items.summary: Prime Intellect stores the MLA latent in NVFP4, shrinking rows from 576 to 352 bytes and fitting about 50% more cached tokens than FP8 ( @PrimeIntellect ).

items.subsection: Inference, Hardware and Systems
items.title: Low-precision benchmarking
items.summary: Stas Bekman measured NVFP4 about 9% more efficient than MXFP4 on B200, with higher accuracy ( @StasBekman ). mamf-finder : The tool now benchmarks FP8, MXFP8, MXFP4 and NVFP4 ( update ).

items.subsection: Inference, Hardware and Systems
items.title: Memory and speed
items.summary: NVHBM moves the memory controller into a custom base die, claiming up to 30% more bandwidth and 15% lower power than HBM4E ( @vikramskr ). Disputed economics : Micron says NVHBM will improve its margins; @vikramskr disputes this ( counterpoint ).
